fields.title: Nothing checks that a suppression is local and justified

sections.What it checks:
* [std-CSSTY.a-suppression-is-local-and-says-why](https://github.com/paul80nd/knowledge-as-code/blob/c32ef7e752de946ec0ebf6d1dadc53305cf06df5/examples/engineering/standards/platform/dotnet/code-style.md#a-suppression-is-local-and-says-why) says a suppression "**MUST** sit on the member it applies to, with a
  `Justification` giving the reason".
* It says a repository "**MUST NOT** disable a rule in `.editorconfig` to clear a warning in one file".
sections.How it works:
Nothing runs. The check these rules need is a pipeline job over the lines a pull request adds. It fails on any of these:

* `#pragma warning disable`
* a `<NoWarn>` element in a project file
* a `dotnet_diagnostic.<id>.severity = none` line in `.editorconfig`
* a `[SuppressMessage(` with no `Justification =`, or one with an `assembly:` target

The same patterns can run over the staged diff as a pre-commit check, or over the written content as a Claude Code hook on `Write` and `Edit`.
sections.Coverage and gaps:
A reviewer reading the diff is the only thing that notices a blanket suppression today.

The check proves a `Justification` is present, and a reviewer still judges whether it gives a reason. A `.editorconfig` severity change may be a deliberate rule for the whole repository. The check fails it anyway, and a reviewer decides. An attribute split across lines passes a pattern that reads one line.
